subject: Day 69: varied-tempo live music
bodyText:
Today's focus
Tempo and rhythm discrimination is sharpening this week. Today is about stretching Avi's perceptual range with live, varied-tempo singing before it narrows to the rhythms he hears most.

Action items
- Sing live to him in a tempo sequence today (a slow lullaby, then a fast clapping song, then slow again); live participatory music, not recordings, is the active ingredient tied to earlier rhythm and pitch discrimination. Gerry, Unrau and Trainor 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Take a 20-to-30-minute daylight stroller loop for fresh air and parental cardiovascular recovery; keep giving the 400 IU/day vitamin D supplement regardless, since breastfed infants need it independent of sun exposure. AAP HealthyChildren: vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- If you and Anoushka have not yet, talk through the first-birthday venue and date now, since top Bay Area venues book 6 to 9 months out.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Quiet startle to loud sounds and reactive head-turns toward voices; both are expected and reassuring.
- [monitor] Persistent head asymmetry (positional plagiocephaly) despite repositioning; ask about PT or repositioning advice at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Decreased feeding over 24 hours or more, or any new color change during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 immediately for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Sing a slow lullaby, then a fast clapping song, then slow again; varying tempo live preserves the perceptual range as his rhythm discrimination sharpens. Gerry, Unrau and Trainor 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Add a book with a repeated refrain to the rotation; the predictable pattern drives early predictive language processing alongside the novel titles. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Fit in a daylight stroller loop for varied sensory input and vitamin D, keeping the 400 IU/day supplement going since outdoor time does not replace it for breastfed infants. AAP HealthyChildren: vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; keep the wind-down sequence consistent.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
- Around week 14-18: the 4-month sleep regression typically begins, often alongside the first roll.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
